::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Febry 3d [1866]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Katherine Wykes-Sneyd
:::

My dear [Henrietta](people/person_538.qmd)
I believe Goosedom is to be revived in the new members, not that new ones are ever so good as old. The two first proposed are accepted, and I hope your [Lilian](people/person_1008.qmd) will be, but you will hear from the [Secretary](people/person_329.qmd).[^1] I am afraid I did not find her out at the Patteson’s party.[^2] We shall have to make a new arrangement as to circulation which you shall hear in the next Cackle when it is matured

 yo
[signature cut out]

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: The two new members of the [Gosling Society](organizations/other_104.qmd) were [Frances Mary Peard](people/person_1160.qmd) and [Florence Wilford](people/person_1520.qmd).
[^3]: The Pattesons were [Joan](people/person_1154.qmd) and [Fanny Patteson](people/person_1151.qmd), who lived at Torquay, not far from Lilian Mitchell's home at Kingsteignton.
